claims.claim: A selected package.json that fails JSON parsing must produce an error finding.
claims.trigger: An existing package.json is selected for validation and JSON.parse fails.
claims.exceptions: A selected path that does not exist returns no finding; do not conflate this with malformed hook input. Already registered XML quoted-attribute and NUL decoding rules are not asserted as new.
claims.enforcement_effect: Error finding, CLI exit 1 when returned; post-tool dispatcher reports the finding as feedback rather than an internal hook crash.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Coverage explicitly describes the error but classifies it IMPLEMENTATION. Registered validation timing and hook-input failure policy do not express this manifest validity/readability condition.
Version/CPM requirements concern values in readable parsed manifests; the specific failure-to-inspect condition is only attributed as a mechanism.

Missing-file success, NUL decoding rejection and the minimal XML grammar are registered. None requires the selected manifest failure here to produce an error finding. JSON parsing and filesystem read failure differ from each of those triggers.

claims.comparison_reason: The error condition can occur without any detectable dependency/version violation. Both Claude runs describe but dismiss it as implementation; union search found no equivalent registered error condition.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A selected package.json with trailing comma errors even if its only dependency has an exact approved stable version.
claims.confidence: HIGH source behavior; MEDIUM-HIGH effective-constraint interpretation
